parsed.narrative: GM Tom Ross of Soledad Township had been in hot action in the Southwest Pacific fighting on PT Boats against Japanese submarines. He had two PT Boats shot out from under him and he received awards for heroism. He was reported Missing In Action at age 19.

Robert Fose (an only son) of Newhall served aboard the famous cruiser USS Boise and was killed in action on October 12, 1943, with a total of 107 sailors during the fierce Battle of Cape Esperance near Guadalcanal. The USS Boise was repaired and returned action in June 1944. Robert Fose is buried at Valhalla Cemetery in Burbank, Calif.

Notes: Robert Cone was a member of the Cone family that owned the Saugus Cafe for 86 years. His death in World War II is mentioned in his brother Dick Cone's obituary and in a newspaper article about Tom Ross, who was missing in action.

SGT Ozal Smart of Castaic enlisted in the US Army at Fort MacArthur, Calif., on September 27, 1940 and served with the 17th Airborne Division. 1st Lt. Jack Nims: "He was released over the landing zone at 1115 hours and was last seen as he entered the smoke over the LZ and was not observed after that." SGT Smart, at age 34, was reported killed in action near Wesel, Germany, and is buried at the American War Cemetery Margraten. SGT Smart was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart.

parsed.remains: Burial at sea(?); headstone or cenotaph at Inglewood Park Cemetery (Calif.)
parsed.narrative: S2C Perry Leon Cherry of Newhall served aboard the U.S.S. Thatcher in the South Pacific and Central Pacific. While in the Central Pacific at the Marshall Islands at age 19, was killed in a gunnery accident in performance of his duty. He was likely buried at sea in the Pacific Ocean.

parsed.unit: Company B, 110th Infantry Regiment, 28th Infantry Division
parsed.remains: Buried in an American Military Cemetery in France; repatriated in 1949; final resting place Valhalla Cemetery, North Hollywood
parsed.narrative: PVT John Amos Ward fought with the 110th Infantry Regiment,
Johnny Cordova of Castaic was killed in action on Okinawa June 18, 1945. He is listed as DOW (Died Of Wounds), meaning he was wounded and later died.

Jim Bartlett of Soledad Township enlisted in the US Army in January 1943 and was trained for aerial photography. At age 29, Bartlett was aboard a US Transport ship in the Mediterranean Sea — probably the SS Paul Hamilton — when it was struck by an aerial torpedo on April 20, 1944.

parsed.remains: Ardennes American Cemetery, Neupré, Belgium (Plot D Row 6 Gravce 38)
parsed.narrative: SSG James M. Redmond of Soledad Township was killed in action during savage fighting in Belgium. His outfit was previously in the thick of operations on D-Day, June 1944, and his group received a citation for slashing a 50-yard gap through barbed wire, underwater obstacles and mines on the coast of Normandy when the big push started. SSG Redmond had participated in battles in France and Holland.

2LT Jack Harland at age 28 was the copilot of a B-24 that collided in midair with another B-24 and crashed near Gate, Okla., during a training exercise on March 31, 1944. His status is DNB, Died Non-Battle.

PVT Garry Wingfield of Soledad Township served with the 31st Infantry Regiment and was killed in action June 13, 1942. PVT Wingfield was awarded the Bronze Star and Purple Heart. He is buried in the Manila American Cemetery, Manila, Philippines.

parsed.casualtyDate: MIA; Lost at Sea or Buried at Sea, August 11, 1950; presumed dead December 31, 1953
parsed.remains: unrecovered; memorialized in Court 8, Courts of the Missing, Honolulu Memorial
parsed.narrative: CPL Thomas was a member of the 8036th Signal Service Company. At age 20, he was listed as Missing In Action while fighting the enemy in South Korea on August 11, 1950. He was officially presumed dead December 31, 1953. His remains were not recovered. His name is inscribed on the Courts of the Missing at the Honolulu Memorial. CPL Thomas was awarded the Purple Heart, the Korean Service Medal, the United Nations Service Medal, the National Defense Service Medal, the Korean Presidential Unit Citation and the Republic of Korea War Service Medal.

parsed.highSchool: Wm. S. Hart High, Class of 1951
parsed.narrative: PFC Morissett of Saugus was a Light Weapons Infantryman with the 25th Infantry Division. At age 19, he was killed in action while fighting in South Korea on March 30, 1951. He was hit in the head and chest by enemy fire and died instantly. PFC Morissett was awarded the Purple Heart, the Combat Infantryman's Badge, the Korean Service Medal, the United Nations Service Medal, the National Defense Service Medal, the Korean Presidential Unit Citation and the Republic of Korea War Service Medal.

MSG Montenegro of Newhall served with the 19th Infantry Regiment, 24th Infantry Division. At age 36, he was killed in action while fighting the enemy in South Korea on February 8, 1951. MSG Montenegro was awarded the Purple Heart, the Combat Infantryman Badge, the Korean Service Medal, the United Nations Service Medal, the National Defense Service Medal, the Korean Presidential Unit Citation and the Republic of Korea War Service Medal.
Private Acuna was reported Missing In Action on July 31, 1950. The fact of his death was ascertained two and a half months later. Approximately a year after his death,

parsed.remains: unrecovered; memorialized in Court 8, Courts of the Missing, Honolulu Memorial
parsed.narrative: ENS Kelly of Newhall was a pilot of an AD-3 Skyraider dive bomber assigned to Fighter Squadron 54 aboard the carrier USS Essex. At age 23, during a combat mission over North Korea on January 9, 1952, his aircraft was struck by anti-aircraft fire, nosed over in a vertical dive, crashed and burned. ENS Kelly's remains were not recovered. His name is inscribed on the Courts of the Missing at the Honolulu Memorial. For leadership and valor, ENS Raymond Gene Kelly was awarded the Distinguished Flying Cross, Air Medal with Gold Star, the Purple Heart, the Combat Action Ribbon, the Korean Service Medal, the United Nations Service Medal, the National Defense Service Medal, the Korean Presidential Unit Citation and the Republic of Korea War Service Medal.

A former Hart High School student, PFC Robert L. Whisler served in the 8th Cavalry Regiment, 1st Cavalry Division. He was sent to South Korea on July 16, 1950, and immediately went to the front lines. PFC Whisler was killed in action while fighting the enemy in South Korea on September 3, 1950. The details of his death, at age 19, are unknown. PFC Whisler was awarded the Combat Infantryman Badge, Korean Service Medal, National Defense Medal, Republic of Korea Presidential Unit Citation, Republic of Korea War Service Medal and the United Nations Service Medal.

SSG Brian Cody Prosser of Frazier Park was a Green Beret soldier assigned to the 3rd Battalion, 5th Special Forces Group. At age 28, SSG Prosser was killed by friendly fire when an Air Force B-52 dropped a 1-ton bomb after an airstrike was called in on nearby Taliban forces in Kandahar, Afghanistan, on December 5, 2001. The bomb fell about 100 yards from the

parsed.unit: 272nd Military Police Company, 21st Theater Support Command
parsed.remains: Cremated; ashes scattered on hiking trails
parsed.narrative: PFC Cole W. Larsen of Canyon Country served with the 272nd Military Police Company in and around Baghdad and Fallujah, Iraq. During his second tour of duty at age 19, while escorting fellow soldiers on November 13, 2004, a civilian truck collided with his armored military vehicle causing it to roll over and kill him. PFC Larsen had been awarded the Bronze Star. He is memorialized with a cenotaph at Eternal Valley Cemetery in Newhall, Calif.

SGT Dean Todd was a satellite communications expert with the 307th Signal Battalion in South Korea. He was notified of a promotion and transfer to MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, Fla. On August 30, 2004, approximately two weeks before his scheduled departure to Florida, SGT Todd committed suicide. He was 21.

parsed.remains: Forest Lawn Memorial Park, Glendale, Calif.
parsed.narrative: SGT Dennis L. Sellen Jr. of Newhall, at age 20, served with the 1st Battalion, 185th Infantry Regiment and was killed in gun accident near the Kuwaiti border in Umm al Qasr, Iraq, on February 11, 2007. Reportedly, a fellow soldier accidentally discharged his weapon while cleaning it after a combat mission.

parsed.highSchool: Wm. S. Hart High, Class of 2002
parsed.unit: 782nd Brigade Support Battalion, 4th Brigade Combat Team, 82nd Airborne Division
parsed.remains: San Fernando Mission Cemetery, Mission Hills
parsed.narrative: SGT Ian Timothy D. Gelig of Stevenson Ranch served as an armored-vehicle driver assigned to the 782nd Brigade Support Battalion, 4th Brigade Combat Team, 82nd Airborne Division. At age 25, SGT Gelig was killed March 1, 2010, when a suicide bomber drove into his convoy in southern Afghanistan's Kandahar province, on the Pakistani border. Sgt. Gelig's commendations include the Bronze Star, Army Commendation Medal, Purple Heart, the Army Good Conduct Medal, the National Defense Service Medal, the Afghanistan Campaign Medal with Campaign Star, the Global War on Terrorism Medal, the Army Service Ribbon, the Overseas Service Ribbon, the Basic Parachutist Badge, and the NATO Medal. SGT Gelig is buried at the San Fernando Mission Cemetery in Mission Hills, Calif.

parsed.unit: 3rd Battalion, 3rd Marine Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, III Marine Expeditionary Force
parsed.remains: Section A Site 2160, Veterans Memorial Park, 17111 S. Camp Williams Road, Bluffdale, Salt Lake County, Utah
parsed.narrative: PFC Jake Suter of Stevenson Ranch served with the 3rd Marine Division. He was killed May 29, 2010, at age 18 while supporting combat operations in Helmand province, Afghanistan on the Pakistani border, exactly one year after graduating from West Ranch High School and less than one week into his tour in Afghanistan. PFC Suter is buried at Utah Veterans Memorial Park.

SGT John Michael Conant of Saugus was a 15-year veteran of the US Army who served with the 4th Infantry Division. He served two tours of duty in Iraq as a combat medic. SGT Conant died in Colorado Springs on Thursday, April 10, 2008; circumstances are unknown. SGT Conant is buried at the Punchbowl National Cemetery in Honolulu, Hawaii.
PFC José Ricardo Flores-Mejia of Santa Clarita served with the 25th Transportation Company, 25th Infantry Division.

parsed.unit: 1st Battalion, 3rd Marines, 3rd Marine Division, III Marine Expeditionary Force
parsed.narrative: LCpl Richard P. Slocum of Saugus joined the Marine Corps right out of high school and served in a combat role with the 3rd Marine Division in Iraq. At age 19, he was killed while manning a machine gun in the turret of a Humvee when it accidentally crashed while trying to avoid a barrier near Abu Gharib, Iraq, on October 24, 2004. LCpl Slocum is buried at Eternal Valley Cemetery in Newhall, Calif.
PFC Wilson of Santa Clarita served with the 82nd Airborne Division and was headed overseas when he died in an automobile accident in North Carolina on August 13, 2002, at age 19.

SP4 Rudy A. Acosta of Canyon Country served as an Army Medic with the 2nd Stryker Calvary Regiment in Kandahar, Afghanistan where he was fatally shot at age 20 by a rogue Afghani security soldier on March 19, 2011. SP4 Rudy Acosta was awarded the Bronze Star and Purple Heart among numerous other citations. His rank was elevated posthumously to SP4 from PFC. SP4 Acosta is buried at Eternal Valley Cemetery in Newhall, Calif.

parsed.narrative: SP4 Stephen E. Colley of Valencia served in Iraq with the 4th Infantry Division. While on base, he committed suicide May 16, 2007, six months after returning from a tour in Iraq.

PVT Albert Lee Moore of Soledad Township enlisted in the US Army Infantry in July 1941 and became a member of the 25th Infantry Division. He lost his life in the Pacific area; details are not known other than his unit had been sent to relieve the Marines at Guadalcanal. His status is DNB, Died Non-Battle. PVT Moore is buried at Forest Lawn Cemetery, Glendale, Calif.

parsed.remains: Avery Memorial Cemetery, Avery, Lincoln County, Okla. (Right of front gate, near front)
parsed.narrative: PFC Arch Beall of Newhall joined the US Army's 394th Infantry Regiment and was killed in action on March 13, 1945. Details are unknown.

parsed.remains: North Africa American Cemetery in Cartago (Carthage), Tunisia

CPL Lawrence E. Kenaston was a veteran of Guadalcanal, and six weeks after his return home took his own life at his stepsister's house in Newhall. He was 34.
SGT Eugene E. Darr of Saugus served with the 96th Infantry Division and at age 22 was killed in action June 10, 1945 on Okinawa. SGT Darr was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart.
SoM Frank Whitmore of Soledad Township was killed October 9, 1943, while serving aboard the destroyer USS Buck when it was sunk by a German U-Boat off of Salerno, Italy.
